tasks.title: Set up the shared project repository
tasks.description: Create one GitHub repository that can be used safely from the desktop and laptop without relying on OneDrive.
acceptance_criteria: The project is stored outside OneDrive
The local main branch is connected to GitHub
Changes can be pushed on one computer and pulled on the other

tasks.title: Prepare the local Python workspace
tasks.description: Create an isolated Python environment and install the libraries the first version of the project will need.
acceptance_criteria: The project uses Python 3.12
The virtual environment starts correctly
The required libraries install without errors
The virtual environment is not uploaded to GitHub
tasks.notes: The dependency list can be simplified later when the main project structure is created.

tasks.title: Create a visual project board
tasks.description: Replace the difficult-to-read Markdown task list with a visual board that saves task changes into Git.
acceptance_criteria: Tasks can be moved between To do, Doing, and Done
Tasks can be created and edited
Changes are saved to project_board/tasks.json
The board runs locally on both computers
tasks.notes: Use the Create task button at the top of the board to add your own work items.

tasks.title: Get the local database and file storage running
tasks.description: Set up the two local services that will hold the project data: a database for organized information and search results, and file storage for untouched copies of imported textbook material.
acceptance_criteria: One command starts both services
The project can connect to both services
Stored data remains available after the services restart
Passwords and local data are not uploaded to GitHub
A simple health check clearly says whether everything is working
tasks.notes: This is the recommended next task.

tasks.title: Agree on how we will import the first textbook
tasks.description: Confirm the official source, license, exact version, and first chapters of The Nature of Code before downloading any content. We should use the official source files instead of blindly scraping the rendered website.
acceptance_criteria: The official source and website are recorded
The license and required attribution are recorded
The exact book version can be identified later
The first import is limited to the Introduction and Chapters 0–2
The import can be repeated on another computer
tasks.notes: This prevents us from building the importer around an unreliable or unauthorized source.

tasks.title: Import the first chapters of The Nature of Code
tasks.description: Download the Introduction and Chapters 0–2 from the approved official source and preserve an untouched local copy before processing it.
acceptance_criteria: The selected chapters download successfully
The untouched source files are stored locally
The source version and download time are recorded
Running the import twice does not create duplicate books or chapters
The import reports what it found and any failures
tasks.notes: This is the first real content entering the system.

tasks.title: Turn the imported files into an organized digital textbook
tasks.description: Read the imported source files and store the book in a clear hierarchy so the system knows which text and code belong to each chapter and section.
acceptance_criteria: The book title and source information are stored
Chapters and sections appear in the correct order
Paragraphs and code examples remain attached to the correct section
Every section keeps a link to the original source
The stored content can be inspected without reading raw database rows
tasks.notes: The goal is a trustworthy digital copy, not search yet.

tasks.title: Break the textbook into useful searchable passages
tasks.description: Divide each section into passages that are small enough to search but large enough to retain meaning. Code examples and closely related explanations should stay together.
acceptance_criteria: Passages do not mix unrelated sections
Code examples are not cut in half
Each passage remembers its book, chapter, section, and source link
Passage size can be changed through configuration
A human can inspect sample passages and understand them
tasks.notes: Good passage boundaries are essential for good answers later.

tasks.title: Make the textbook searchable
tasks.description: Create a search system that finds passages both by exact wording and by meaning, then combines those results into one useful ranked list.
acceptance_criteria: Exact terms such as function names can be found
Questions written differently from the textbook can still find relevant sections
Results show the chapter, section, source link, and search score
Search can be limited to a selected book or chapter
A short set of sample questions returns sensible passages
tasks.notes: This task includes connecting the local embedding model and combining keyword and meaning-based search.

tasks.title: Let us test textbook search from the terminal
tasks.description: Create a simple command where we type a question and immediately see the most relevant textbook passages and their source links.
acceptance_criteria: A question can be entered from the terminal
The most relevant passages are printed in order
Every result includes the book, chapter, section, and source link
Optional details explain why each passage ranked where it did
The command provides a clear error if the database or local model is unavailable
tasks.notes: This lets us evaluate retrieval before asking an AI model to write answers.

tasks.title: Answer questions with the local AI model and show sources
tasks.description: Send the retrieved textbook passages to a local model, generate a useful explanation, and show exactly which sections support the answer.
acceptance_criteria: The local model answers using the retrieved textbook passages
The answer includes inspectable source links
The model admits when the textbook does not contain enough information
Outside knowledge is not presented as if it came from the book
The response records the model used and how long it took
tasks.notes: Completing this task finishes the first major product milestone.

tasks.title: Check whether search and answers are actually reliable
tasks.description: Create a small set of questions with known textbook answers and use it to find weak search results, unsupported claims, and incorrect citations.
acceptance_criteria: The test set covers facts, explanations, code, and unanswerable questions
Each question identifies the expected supporting section
Search quality and citation correctness are measured separately
Failures can be inspected rather than hidden behind one score
The results tell us what should be improved next
tasks.notes: Do this before adding many new product features.

tasks.title: Add useful study modes
tasks.description: Turn the basic question-answer system into a study companion with explanation, guided questioning, quizzes, and code walkthroughs.
acceptance_criteria: Explain mode can adjust the level of detail
Socratic mode gives hints before revealing the answer
Quiz mode creates questions from selected chapters
Code walkthrough mode connects code to the textbook explanation
Every mode continues to show textbook sources
tasks.notes: Only start this after grounded answers work reliably.

tasks.title: Create a browser interface for studying
tasks.description: Build a simple browser experience where a learner can choose a book and chapter, ask questions, inspect sources, and use the study modes.
acceptance_criteria: A learner can select a book and chapter
Questions and answers stream in the browser
Sources open to the relevant textbook section
Retrieved passages can be inspected for debugging
The interface remains usable on a laptop screen
tasks.notes: The underlying search and answer services should already work before this begins.

tasks.title: Prove the system works with a second textbook
tasks.description: Import Dive into Deep Learning and verify that the same workflow works without rebuilding the system specifically for that book.
acceptance_criteria: The second book uses the same import stages
Both books use the same search and answer system
Book-specific handling stays isolated
Users can choose which book or books to search
Licenses and attributions remain correct for both books
tasks.notes: This is where the project becomes a reusable textbook platform instead of a one-book demo.

tasks.title: Compare local and hosted AI models fairly
tasks.description: Give different models the same question and the same textbook passages, then compare answer quality, speed, and cost without changing the evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Every model receives identical retrieved passages
Answer quality and source faithfulness are recorded
Speed and API cost are recorded where applicable
Results can be repeated from saved configuration
The comparison explains its limitations
tasks.notes: This supports the final portfolio and research story.
